Hi all,

Reviewed Acme's counter. Below is our recommended approach — practical, defensible, and tailored for procurement. Summary first, then proposed language.

Summary (position):
- Keep a mutual exclusion of consequential, special, incidental and punitive damages as the baseline. One-way exclusions materially increase Redwood's risk and are not acceptable without significant commercial trade-offs (much higher cap, additional credit, or indemnities).
- Carveouts: accept carveouts where necessary: (i) breach of confidentiality/PI obligations; (ii) IP infringement; (iii) willful misconduct/gross negligence; (iv) obligations to pay amounts due under Order Form (fees).
- Definition: adopt a defined list of illustrative examples for "consequential damages" (e.g., loss of profits, loss of business, loss of use) and make clear that direct/actual damages (reasonable cost to remediate, fees) remain recoverable up to the cap.
- Punitive/exemplary: include an explicit waiver of punitive/exemplary damages (these are not recoverable by either party).

Trade options if Acme insists on one-way:
- Option A (commercial): Accept one-way exclusion only if cap is increased to 2x the standard and Redwood gets an explicit indemnity for IP claims; OR
- Option B (credit): Keep mutual exclusion and offer a one-time implementation credit (5-10% of first-year committed spend) to help procurement sign-off.

Proposed language (single-paragraph redline friendly):
"Except with respect to (a) a party's breach of its confidentiality or personal data obligations, (b) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (c) infringement of a party's intellectual property rights, and (d) amounts payable under any Order Form, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO LOST PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS, LOSS OF USE OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. FOR CLARITY, DIRECT DAMAGES (INCLUDING REASONABLE COSTS TO REMEDY BREACHES AND PAYMENTS DUE UNDER AN ORDER FORM) SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE LIABILITY CAP SET FORTH IN THE APPLICABLE ORDER FORM."

Notes: this preserves a mutual exclusion, explicitly lists common procurement examples, and carves out critical exceptions. If Acme insists on one-way, push for Option A or B above.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with Jane + procurement to walk through.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
